sources.claim: Live venomous Wagler's pit vipers sit openly in the Snake Temple; legend says incense makes them docile; entrance is free.
Snake Temple in Bayan Lepas honours Chor Soo Kong; pit vipers rest around the altar but are fewer than in the past.
Penang War Museum is a haunted dark-tourism site with bat-filled tunnels and ghost stories of executioner Tadashi Suzuki; historian disputes parts of narrative.
Penang War Museum charges about RM38 for foreign adults and is open 9am-6pm daily.
Penang War Museum is the largest war museum in Southeast Asia, on the former British Batu Maung Fort with tunnels and barracks.
Penang War Museum is described as the most haunted museum in Asia, gaining fame after a 2013 National Geographic documentary.
Kek Lok Si features a seven-storey Pagoda of Ten Thousand Buddhas combining Chinese, Thai and Burmese architectural styles.
Crag Hotel on Penang Hill, a Japanese WWII POW prison and former Uplands School, was a film set for Indochine and Indian Summers and lies in ruins as of 2026.
The abandoned Crag Hotel sits on an isolated part of Penang Hill with little sign of its former glory.
Caledonia 99-Door House: owner John St Maur Ramsden shot dead on the staircase in 1948, murder unsolved, fuelling haunting rumours.
Urban-exploration mapping lists 900+ abandoned places across Penang state.
Wonderfood Museum displays replicas of over 100 types of local street food at larger-than-life scale.
Ghost Museum Penang showcases folklore creatures such as pontianak, jiang shi and Ju-on.
At the Upside Down Museum furniture is mounted on the ceiling so visitors photograph themselves apparently falling upward.
Made In Penang Interactive Museum is the island's first large 3D trick-art gallery near the jetty with about 30 illusion paintings.
Monkey Cup Garden on Penang Hill grows ~100 species of carnivorous Nepenthes pitcher plants; entry RM5 (~EUR1).
TeddyVille Museum holds Malaysia's first and largest teddy-bear collection at DoubleTree Resort, Tanjung Tokong.
Penang's interactive museums are deliberately playful rather than solemn heritage displays.
Wild Nepenthes pitcher plants grow on Penang Hill slopes reached on the climb from the Botanic Gardens.
Night boat rides at Sungai Kerian / Nibong Tebal on the Penang mainland pass mangroves lit by thousands of fireflies.
George Town speakeasies include Hold Up! (orange-fridge door) and Magazine 63 (hidden wooden door).
Hin Bus Depot, a derelict 1940s bus terminus, was revived in 2014 as an indie art and events space.
Hin Bus Depot was converted from a derelict bus depot into an art gallery and community space.
The 2009 Marking George Town / Voices from the People project installed 52 steel-rod caricatures explaining historic street names.
Ernest Zacharevic's interactive murals incorporate real objects; his Boy on a Motorbike uses an actual repurposed motorbike.
Penang Heritage Joss Stick Maker, founded c.1948 by Lee Beng Chuan, is continued by his son using sandalwood, agarwood and Tibet holy grass.
Haja Mohideen Mohammed Shariff is reportedly the only remaining songkok maker in George Town, hand-sewing since 1962.
George Town World Heritage Inc documents the city's surviving heritage trades and artisans.
Balik Pulau's hilly terrain produces durians with stronger aroma, thicker flesh and richer flavour.
Penang durian farm buffets/stay-and-eat passes let visitors taste rare cultivars including a numbing variety.
A Michelin Bib Gourmand Penang curry mee is served with cubes of coagulated pork (formerly duck) blood in coconut broth.
Pig's organ soup is a peppery broth of pork offal including liver, heart, intestine, kidney, stomach, tongue, lung and blood curd.
Wat Chayamangkalaram (founded 1845) holds a ~33m reclining Buddha that doubles as a columbarium, opposite the Dhammikarama Burmese Temple.
Dhammikarama Burmese Temple (1803) is the only Burmese Buddhist temple in Malaysia, facing the Thai reclining Buddha temple.
Kek Lok Si, Malaysia's largest Buddhist temple, has a 30.2m bronze Guanyin statue completed in 2002.
Kek Lok Si has a turtle Liberation Pond where pilgrims release turtles to gain merit.
The Tanjung Bungah mosque is built on stilts and appears to float on water at high tide; opened 2007, holds 1,500 worshippers.
Masjid Terapung is Malaysia's first mosque built over the open sea and replaced a mosque destroyed by the 2004 tsunami.
Penang's Hungry Ghost Festival features tall blue-faced King of Hell (Tai Su Yeah) paper-and-rattan effigies that are ritually burned.
In May 2026 Penang's Hungry Ghost Festival was entered into the state heritage gazette as a step toward UNESCO recognition.
Thaipusam 2026 falls on 1 February at the Waterfall Hill Temple with a new kavadi permit system for crowd control.
Thaipusam devotees carry peacock-feather kavadis pierced into the skin behind a silver chariot at the Waterfall Hill temple.
Specialist kavadi piercers perform the Thaipusam skewer-and-hook piercings safely and reportedly painlessly.
